chunks: And by this chain of narration, from al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from his brother al-Hasan, from Zur'ah, from Sama'ah ibn Mihran, from Abu 'Abd Allah (peace be upon him), who said:
When a man is in a state of janabah and inserts his hand into a vessel, there is no harm — if no semen has touched his hand.

key_terms.الْإِنَاءِ: vessel/container (specifically for water used in ritual purification)
key_terms.الْمَنِيِّ: semen (one of the a'yan al-najasah, intrinsically impure substances)
key_terms.جَنَابَةٌ: janabah (major ritual impurity requiring ghusl, arising from intercourse or seminal emission)
key_terms.فَلَا بَأْسَ: there is no harm / no objection (standard Shia jurisprudential formula indicating permissibility)

ai.seo_question: Does inserting the hand of a person in a state of janabah into a vessel of water render the water najis, according to Imam al-Sadiq (AS)?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (AS) issues a legal ruling that a man in a state of janabah who inserts his hand into a vessel of water does not render that water ritually impure, on the condition that no semen is physically present on his hand. Recorded in al-Istibsar in the chapter on small quantities of water that may be contaminated by najasah, this ruling establishes that the state of janabah itself does not transfer najasah to water — only the physical presence of a najis substance does.
